faq.a: Aid is associated with the Arabic form عَايِد, whose core sense is aid; returning, visitor.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aid?
faq.a: Aid is associated with Arabic. Aid is Arabic عَائِد (ʿĀʾid), the active participle of عَادَ, meaning 'returning, visitor'.
Yes — the underlying form عَايِد is Arabic.
Aid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĀʾid is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Aid is rendered عاید and carries the sense عاید، واپس آنے والا.

faq.q: What does Aid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aid is rendered عاید and carries the sense عاید، بازگشت‌کننده.
A romanized syllable approximation is aid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aid, aid. Script forms are عايد, عاید, عَايِد, आइद.

faq.q: Is Aid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
